# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–9 (Complete and Final – Updated 85)

## Setting and Time
- **Period**: Spring through late August of first year; Christmas/New Year period; nearly three weeks into new year (1832) after Lords threw out Reform Bill; summer and autumn of first year; winter of first year; Vauxhall evening during spring of first year; spring of second year; summer of second year; autumn of second year; winter of second year; **spring of third year (present narrative)** (narrative extends into future years); present day with Fred and Mary at Stone Court in white-haired placidity
- **Primary Locations**: Middlemarch, Lowick, Grange, Freshitt, Mirecombe, Salwick, Quenwick, Fenmere, Bryngate, Chalky Flats, Gulton, Highbury, Cheltenham, Tipton, Yoddrell's farm, Frick, Miremere, Riverston, Quallingham, Halsell Wood, Loamford, Brassing, Stone Court, Coldcombe, St. Peter's Place, Lowick Gate, Shrubs, Dunholt, Yorkshire, Staveton, Bilkley, Harrowgate, Melspring, Wilhaven, Salford, Chiswick Mall, Hammersmith, Soho, Thames, England, Oxford, Chiswick Church, Buxton, Kensington turnpike, Russell Square, London, Southampton Row, Vauxhall, Exeter 'Change, India (Boggley Wollah, Ramgunge, Budgebudge, Calcutta, Dumdum), Forty Thieves theatre, King's 14th regiment post, Highbury Barn, Covent Garden Market, Doctor Swishtail's Seminary, Bedford tavern, Thames Street (City), Royal Gardens, St. George's Hanover Square, Lambeth Palace, Great Gaunt Street, Queen's Crawley (Hants), Mudbury, Gaunt Square, Mansion House, Oxford Street, Swallow Street, Cambridge, Leakington, Squashmore, Bethesda Chapel Liverpool, Naples, Paris, Eton, Pumpernickel, Strasburg, Crawley parish, Yarlton, Quashimaboo, Fuddleston, Roxby, Wapshot Hall, Christchurch, Rectory House, Hampshire, Chiswick, Coldcombe, Huddleston, Cocoa-Tree, Woolwich, hill farms of Coldcombe, Humdrum Hall, Wattier's, Chatham, Horse Guards, Carlton House, St. Kitt's, Opera, Prince Regent locations, Demerara, St. Vincent's, Quebec, Charing Cross, Pall Mall, Old Slaughters', West Indies, Rochester, Chatham barracks, hill farms of Fenmere, Knightsbridge Barracks, Park Lane, Hants, Life Guards, 150th regiment depot at Mudbury, Dunholt village, Bloomsbury, Russell Square, Harrowgate, Great Gaunt Street, village of Yarlton, hill farms of Mirecombe, parsonage, forge, **Brompton, barracks neighbourhood (new), City church, Porteus (location of volume 3)**
- **Narrative Presence**: Narrator warns Vanity Fair is "a very vain, wicked, foolish place, full of all sorts of humbugs and falsenesses and pretensions"; observes human hearts and self-deceptions with ironic sympathy; reflects on marriage bargains mothers and daughters make daily; notes precise timing of events; claims privilege of novelist to peek into characters' minds and understand their secrets; comments sardonically on imprudent marriages, noting "if people only made prudent marriages, what a stop to population there would be"

## Main Characters

**Rebecca Sharp (Mrs. Rebecca / Mrs. Rawdon Crawley)** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Age nineteen; father artist/drawing teacher at Miss Pinkerton's academy; mother French opera-girl
- Small, slight, pale, sandy-haired with large attractive eyes; white slender fingers; very pretty and white hands, soft as satin
- Skilled musician, linguist, artist; speaks French with purity; proficient in globes
- Determined, observant, capable of calculated charm; speaks with slight foreign accent when agitated; nerves of iron; never out of temper
- **Secret Marriage**: **FACT (revealed)**: Rebecca is secretly married to Captain Rawdon Crawley. Marriage occurred in City church in quiet, unobserved manner: Rebecca went to pass forenoon with Amelia in Russell Square; a lady very like her was seen entering church with gentleman with dyed mustachios (Rawdon); after quarter hour's interval, gentleman escorted lady back to hackney-coach; described as "quiet bridal party"
- **How Marriage Occurred**: Not formally detailed but implied to have been quiet, likely with special license; narrator notes "if a woman has a will she will assuredly find a way" and questions who can doubt "the probability of a gentleman marrying anybody," invoking examples of imprudent matches and passionate men unable to control desires
- **Role**: Originally companion and nurse to Miss Crawley at Park Lane residence; indispensable; controlled household and sickroom access; maintained composed appearance
- **Social Manipulations Before Marriage**: Received new gowns, necklace, shawl from Miss Crawley; showed Miss Crawley affection of intimate companion; strategically made acquainted with George's suspicions; used jealousy to advantage; defeated George Osborne through studied coolness and strategic superiority
- **Proposals Received**: (1) Sir Pitt Crawley made explicit marriage proposal following Lady Crawley's death, fell on knees, offered complete liberty and settlement of four thousand a year as widower with Baronetcy; (2) Captain Rawdon Crawley explicitly proposed: "Come as Lady Crawley...Come back and be my wife"
- **Rebecca's Responses to Proposals**: To both, claimed she was already married; confessed in agony of tears, voice choking, handkerchief to eyes, fainting against mantelpiece; performed before Miss Crawley, assuming attitude of humility on knees before Sir Pitt; claimed did not despise honor; appealed to kindness; held handkerchief to eyes; sank pathetically in chair; most of audience melted with her sadness
- **Sir Pitt's Knowledge and Response**: Sir Pitt now knows Rebecca is married but not husband's identity; accepted refusal with coolness and good-humor; offered acceptance of her return as governess with complete liberty; maintains friendship ("you're a good little girl, Becky, and I'm your vriend, mind")
- **Miss Crawley's Response After Proposal Event**: Mollified by refusal; now very liberal and generous; loves Rebecca as daughter; solemnly vowed to love her always; promised to do everything in her power to serve her; embraced Rebecca with almost maternal kindness; will set up Rebecca's "gentleman" in shop, commission portrait, speak to cousin Bishop, dote on Becky, arrange wedding with Miss Briggs as bridesmaid; expressed enthusiasm about doing something for family; will not hear of Rebecca's departure; as long as engagement lasts, attachment prodigious; clings with greatest energy; called Rebecca "dear, artless, tender-hearted, affectionate, incomprehensible creature"; remarked she "would have made a good Lady Crawley"; praised her brains, manners, Montmorency blood
- **Rebecca's Regrets and Plans**: In solitude, Rebecca indulged in proper portion of regret for lost opportunity; reflected "I might have been my lady!...I might have led that old man whither I would...I would have had the handsomest carriage in London, and a box at the opera; and I would have been presented next season. All this might have been; and now--now all was doubt and mystery." However, being young lady of resolution, quickly turned attention to future
- **Recent Communications with Rawdon**: Wrote letters to Rawdon addressed to "Miss Eliza Styles" (claimed old schoolfellow with whom resumed correspondence); letters fetched from saddler's by "Miss Eliza Styles," who was actually Captain Rawdon Crawley in disguise (wearing brass spurs and large curling mustachios)
- **The Plan**: When Becky told Rawdon "the great crisis was near, and the time for action had arrived," he expressed readiness to act under her orders as if under colonel's command. Rawdon met Rebecca "in the usual place" next day; Rebecca had determined they must fly and reside in quiet lodgings at Brompton or barracks neighbourhood. Rawdon "had been entreating her to take this measure for weeks past"; was "only too happy" at resolve
- **Rawdon's Preparations**: Pranced off to engage lodgings at two guineas week; ordered piano and half nursery-house of flowers; sent shawls, kid gloves, silk stockings, gold French watches, bracelets, perfumery with "profusion of blind love and unbounded credit"; afterward dined nervously at club waiting for "great moment of his life"
- **Current Status (Spring of Third Year)**: About to flee to Brompton lodgings with Rawdon; Miss Crawley and Briggs remain unaware of Rebecca's marriage; Rebecca's secret still hidden; sang more sweetly than ever in Park Lane, twined herself round Miss Crawley's heart, spoke lightly and laughingly of Sir Pitt's proposal, ridiculed it as foolish fancy of old man, declared she desired no other lot than remain forever with Miss Crawley. Miss Crawley declared she does not intend to let Rebecca stir for years and insisted Rebecca must stay to "take care of the old woman"

**Captain Rawdon Crawley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Captain (described as "major" in marriage license context) in Life Guards; celebrated "blood" or dandy; expert boxer, rat-hunter, four-in-hand driver; very large, six feet high; generous; over head and ears in debt; known gambler, drunkard, profligate
- Miss Crawley almost adopted him; designated for fifty thousand pounds in will
- **Love for Rebecca**: Completely victimized; barbed shaft penetrated his dull hide; raves about her; faced perpetual defeats in romantic campaign; perpetually routed; recognized Mrs. Bute's matchmaking scheme
- **Marriage**: Secretly married to Rebecca in City church (as detailed above); marriage occurred by quiet license without fanfare
- **Proposal to Rebecca**: Following Lady Crawley's death, explicitly proposed: "Come as Lady Crawley, if you like...Come back and be my wife. Your vit vor't. Birth be hanged. You're as good a lady as ever I see...Will you come? Yes or no?" Rebecca's response was acceptance through marriage rather than explicit verbal acceptance
- **Recent Activity**: Won two hundred pounds from George Osborne at billiards at Cocoa-Tree; invited Osborne to dinners; praised horsemanship; introduced to fashionable young men; watched Rebecca's coolness to Osborne; confided George's suspicions about Rebecca; laughed at Osborne's assessments. Since marriage: communicated with Rebecca via letters addressed to "Miss Eliza Styles"; met her "in the usual place"; expressed implicit faith in Rebecca's judgment; agreed to everything she proposed regarding Miss Crawley; described Rebecca as having "head enough for both of us"; "You're sure to get us out of the scrape"; stated "I never saw your equal, and I've met with some clippers in my time too"
- **Current Status (Spring of Third Year)**: Engaged lodgings at Brompton at two guineas weekly; furnished with piano, flowers, luxury items; awaiting moment to unite with Rebecca; waits nervously at club for elopement

**Miss Crawley** [CHARACTER]
- Inherited large fortune; silly, romantic; very attached to Rawdon; adores imprudent matches; good taste for natural manners and pretty faces
- **Relationship with Rebecca After Proposal Events**: Mollified by refusal; very liberal and generous; loves Rebecca as daughter; solemnly vowed love; promised everything in power to serve her; embraced with maternal kindness; blessed and admired her; enthusiastically offered patronage to Rebecca's "gentleman"; will set up shop, commission portrait, speak to Bishop, arrange wedding with Miss Briggs as bridesmaid; clings with greatest energy; attachment prodigious; love and attention to Rebecca intensified
- **Current Behavior (Spring of Third Year)**: Indulges in utmost luxury of sentiment; in Rebecca's absence, solaces herself with sentimental novels, treating "Little Sharp, with her secret griefs" as heroine of the day. When Rebecca present, sings sweetly, talks pleasantly, twines herself around Miss Crawley's heart. Rebecca ridiculed Sir Pitt's proposal as foolish fancy; eyes filled with tears; declared desire to remain forever with benefactress. Miss Crawley responds: "I don't intend to let you stir for years...Here you stay with me and Briggs...you must stay and take care of the old woman"
- **Ignorance of Marriage**: Remains completely unaware Rebecca is married; believes Rebecca has "previous attachment" to unnamed gentleman; will be "shaken when she first hears the news" according to Rebecca's assessment. However, Rebecca is confident Miss Crawley "dotes upon you so (you naughty, good-for-nothing man), that she would pardon you ANYTHING" and that Rebecca herself holds "next place in her heart"

**Amelia Sedley** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Rebecca's former schoolfriend; small, modest, unaffected; tender heart; timid; sweet modest soul
- **Relationship with George**: Confirmed engagement; believes deeply in George; innocent and trusting; assumes his errands legitimate; loves him completely
- **Actual Behavior**: Leaves home daily; dines abroad six days week; neglected twelve Chiswick friends; made confidante of Laura Martin; promised Laura would live with her when married
- **Letters to George**: Extraordinarily long and passionate; filled large paper sheets crossed with perverseness; whole pages of poetry; underlined words with frantic emphasis; repetitive; doubtful grammar; numerous notes followed him
- **Recent**: Visited briefly with Rebecca when Miss Crawley called on Russell Square; came down with kind smiling looks; blushed kissing Rebecca; impressed Miss Crawley with "sweet blushing face." Rebecca visits Amelia in Russell Square regularly (used as cover for her marriage)
- **Worries**: Unaware of George's financial transaction; worries her poor papa melancholy; sent George tenderest letter with foreboding evil

**George Osborne** [MAJOR CHARACTER]
- Handsome; jolly, sociable; excellent at games, billiards, field-sports, song, parade; adored by men; famous drinker and sparrer
- Over head and ears in debt; known gambler, drunkster, profligate; shot Captain Marker in duel; robbed young Lord Dovedale
- **Engagement to Amelia**: Engaged; furious upon learning regiment knows; admits "I am very fond of Amelia; I adore her"; acknowledges "She's faultless"; took tender leave of Amelia
- **Financial Transaction**: Visited City; received document from Mr. Chopper; exchanged at Hulker & Bullock's for pocketful of money; was "much too elated"
- **Recent**: Won two hundred pounds from Rawdon at billiards at Cocoa-Tree; would have played for anything before Dobbin intervention; Rawdon praised his horsemanship; introduction to fashionable young men elated him. Confided to Rawdon that Rebecca was "a sharp one, a dangerous one, a desperate flirt"; Rawdon agreed laughingly

**Other Characters**
- **Lady Crawley (formerly Rose Dawson)** [DECEASED]: Sir Pitt's wife; died during winter of second year at Wilhaven; feeble, lonely soul; Mr. Crawley tended bedside; she was strengthened by his words and comfort
- **Sir Pitt Crawley**: Old, stumpy, short, vulgar; now widower; made marriage proposal to Rebecca; met refusal with coolness and good-humor; offered her return as governess; now knows Rebecca is married but not to whom; maintains friendly relations
- **Miss Briggs**: Displaced by Rebecca; position now sinecure and derision; witnessed Sir Pitt's proposal through keyhole with Mrs. Firkin; delighted to be readmitted to Miss Crawley's confidential conversation; tried to find out gentleman; cherishes old love letters from writing-master; now deeply attached to Rebecca's cause; heart filled with "unutterable pangs of defeat" when Rebecca vowed to remain with Miss Crawley
- **Mrs. Firkin**: Witnessed proposal with Miss Briggs; wrote to Mrs. Bute Crawley reporting events
- **Old Mr. Osborne**: Wealthy merchant; told George Sedley's affairs look bad
- **Old John Sedley**: Observed leaving banker's parlour looking dismal; family affairs troubled
- **Laura Martin**: Amelia's confidante; promised to live with her when married
- **Mrs. Bute Crawley**: Made confidante by Rawdon; received letter from Mrs. Firkin
- **Captain Dobbin**: Carried off George Osborne from billiards
- **Rose and Violet Crawley**: Young pupils left without companionship during mother's illness

## Critical Facts and Status
- Rebecca is secretly married to Rawdon Crawley; marriage occurred quietly in City church by special license
- Miss Crawley remains completely unaware of Rebecca's marriage; believes only in "previous attachment"
- Sir Pitt knows Rebecca is married but not to whom; maintains friendly relations and has accepted her refusal of his proposal
- Rebecca and Rawdon are prepared to flee to Brompton lodgings; plan already in motion as spring of third year begins
- Rawdon has secured lodgings at two guineas weekly and furnished them luxuriously
- Miss Briggs and Mrs. Firkin witnessed proposal and have spread news; Mrs. Firkin informed Mrs. Bute Crawley
- Miss Crawley now enthusiastically devoted to Rebecca and determined to keep her at Park Lane indefinitely
- Rebecca confident Miss Crawley will pardon Rawdon anything and allow them to live in Park Lane on her money
- George's financial gains coincide with Sedley family troubles; George and Rawdon connected socially through billiards and dinners
- Amelia remains innocent of all developments; trusts George completely
